_readme: MONEY-1373 — the FOURTH template in this directory, and the only one whose
healthy reading is a permanent, literal ZERO.
The other three ask questions about a job: did it write what it selected
(monitor-zero-write.json), how long did it take (monitor-latency-p95.json),
did it run at all (monitor-job-absence.json). This one asks nothing about a
job. It is a TRIPWIRE on an invariant: no Databento writer may ever displace
a DAILY session.
WHY THE INVARIANT HOLDS TODAY. `DATABENTO_SCHEMAS` — the Zod enum the
manifest is parsed against in databento-manifest-logic.ts — has no
`ohlcv-1d` member, so a manifest entry naming a daily schema is refused at
parse time and no harvest or append can produce a daily bar. The session
writer refuses a D1 displacement independently of that and counts the
refusal, which is the number this monitor reads.
So a non-zero value cannot mean 'more daily bars than usual arrived'. It
means a writer path reached the D1 series that no manifest can produce — a
schema added to the enum without the writer being revisited, a hand-run job,
or a mis-mapped timeframe. There is no threshold to pick and no baseline to
learn: `> 0` is the entire condition.
Apply with scripts/ops/datadog/apply-monitors.sh. The metric name IS spelled
out in the query below — apply-monitors.sh supplies placeholders only for
the two job counters — and that second spelling is exactly the hazard
MONEY-1238 fault (a) was: a hand-copied name in a monitor and a `prefix:` in
metrics.ts are two spellings of one fact, and a mismatch is answered by
permanent NO DATA, which on THIS monitor is indistinguishable from a
tripwire that has never tripped. So it is held in agreement by a test:
packages/datadog/__tests__/monitor-agreement.test.ts asserts this rendered
query against EMITTED_DATABENTO_METRICS.displacedD1, imported rather than
retyped.
name: [{{env}}] databento displaced a DAILY session
message:
A Databento writer attempted to displace a DAILY (ohlcv-1d) session in the last day.

THIS COUNTER IS SUPPOSED TO BE ZERO FOREVER. It is a tripwire, not a metric anyone tunes. `DATABENTO_SCHEMAS` (packages/core/src/market-data/databento/databento-manifest-logic.ts) has no `ohlcv-1d` member, so no manifest entry can name a daily schema and no harvest or append run can produce a daily bar. A non-zero value means a writer path reached the D1 series anyway.

Where to look, in order:
  1. Did a schema get added to DATABENTO_SCHEMAS without the session writer being revisited?
  2. Was `databento-harvest` or `databento-append` run by hand with an entry the manifest does not describe?
  3. Is a timeframe being mis-mapped on the way into writeSymbolBatch?

The writer REFUSED the displacement — no daily session was overwritten — so this is not data loss. It is the guard reporting that something tried.

Runbook: docs/reference/databento-harvest-runbook.md
@{{notify}}
_notify_no_data_rationale: FALSE, and it is the opposite call from monitor-job-absence.json for a
reason that is specific to this metric rather than a matter of taste.
ABSENCE IS THE HEALTHY STATE HERE. Both emitters call incrementCounter with
the run's `refusedD1` total, which is 0 on every correct run — and
`databento-harvest` has NO SCHEDULER TRIGGER AT ALL (it is a one-time buy
executed by hand, one manifest entry at a time), so on a normal week the
only writer is the append job. A no-data alarm would therefore page for the
system behaving exactly as designed, which is the muted-alarm shape
NOTHING IS LOST BY TURNING IT OFF. `default_zero()` renders a window with no
points as a real 0, so the threshold still evaluates on silence — and 0 is
the answer we want. And 'databento-append stopped running' is watched by its
own ABSENCE_MONITORS row, which is the instrument for that question.
no_data_timeframe STAYS and is inert, for the reason monitor-latency-p95.json
gives: apply-monitors.sh's render() coerces it to a Number unconditionally,
so deleting the key renders `"no_data_timeframe": null` — a null where
_query_rationale: `sum(last_1d)`, not the job's own window, and not a placeholder. This
monitor is not sized against a cadence: it is a boolean over a counter that
must never move, so the window only decides how long a single tripped run
stays visible. A day is long enough that a breach is not missed between
evaluations and short enough that the alert clears on its own once the cause
NO `job:` FILTER in the query, deliberately. BOTH `databento-harvest` and
`databento-append` emit this counter with their own `job` tag, and the
invariant is a property of the DATA rather than of either job. Filtering to
one would leave the other's breach unwatched; summing across them is the
whole population. `include_tags: true` puts the offending job's tag in the
notification, so the alert still names which one tripped.
`.as_count()` because this is a COUNTER: sum() of a counter without it is a
rate average, which can round a single refusal toward zero — and a single
refusal is the entire event this monitor exists to see.
`thresholds.critical` is 0 to agree with `> 0`; Datadog rejects a monitor
whose threshold disagrees with its query.
_placeholders: {{env}}              Datadog env TAG value — production | qa. NOT the CLI
argument: apply-monitors.sh maps prod -> production via
{{no_data_minutes}}  inert while notify_no_data is false, but must still be
an integer <= 4320 or Datadog refuses the monitor.
{{notify}}           notification handle. The leading `@` is in the message
body above and is the entire routing mechanism — a bare
handle is prose and notifies nobody (MONEY-979).
